editorial: Grief takes a dark turn when a woman seeks solace with her in‑laws in a secluded home, turning an intimate family gathering into an eerie descent toward the supernatural. The film reshapes the concept of a family reunion by mapping the curse to vows held even after death, so that every joke and hair‑raising moment feels like a betrayal of love. Your senses are assaulted by practical gore that feels almost ritualistic, while the score drips with whispered secrets that echo off the cold walls. Pacing glitches in the middle act sometimes let the tension falter before it can catch up again. You’re the type who revels in psychologically‑charged horror that rewards attentive viewing over easy scares.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological horror who appreciate slow‑burn dread.
